title: Cheap Tokens: A Field Guide to Discounted Inference - Andy Nikulin
description:
Andy Nikulin walks through the grey market for discounted AI tokens, from subscription arbitrage to token "transfer stations", and what the discount costs you.

Main Takeaways

- SemiAnalysis got over $11,000 of API-priced tokens from a $200 Anthropic subscription.
- Brokers resell corporate discounts, farmed credits, idle subscriptions and stolen accounts.
- One station sold Gemini 4 Carbon at 55% off within days of launch.
- The catch: swapped models, pricier cached tokens, harvested prompts, deposits that vanish.
- He only uses them for apps that are "not super important and not super secret".

title: Does Your Agent Know "Why"? - David Mihal
description:
David Mihal argues agents need the reasons behind a codebase, not just the code, and shows how Meridian gives them those reasons with architecture decision records (ADRs).

Main Takeaways

- Meridian spent its first month writing only markdown specs, no code.
- With solid specs, the LLM becomes a compiler from English to Rust.
- 212 ADRs since March, about one a day. Some take longer than the code.
- A bad symbol prefix became a permanent ADR, so agents know why odd code exists.
- Setup is an ADR folder, one line in AGENTS.md, and comments citing "ADR 157"

title: Your SaaS Is Becoming an Agent - Sacha Dumay
description:
Sacha Dumay explains why Cashflowy moved its chat from a side panel to the centre of the product, and rebuilt its AI bookkeeper on Vercel's open-source eve.

Main Takeaways

- Users who asked the side-panel chat questions were almost twice as likely to pay.
- His weekend TanStack chat lived in the browser and couldn't run long tasks.
- In eve, user approvals run in code, because an LLM can't be trusted to confirm.
- "Workflow is so outdated." One central agent with 47 tools replaced them.
- Evals run in CI, like the one keeping users from overwriting the ledger.
